description: Two-man army team with the love of Vietnam. Excited to be a participant in one of the famous nasa challenges.
summary:
NextCrop is a crop-rotation decision-support tool for farmers and extension officers in Vietnam. Pick a place on the map and the crop currently grown, and it suggests at least three options, including "keep the current crop", for example a different crop each season or replacing one season with a legume. Each option shows how suitable the land is (FAO GAEZ v5 index, 5 arc-minute cells of about 80 km²), the benefits (nitrogen fixation, a break in pest and disease cycles) and the risks, in plain language, in Vietnamese and English.

A NASA tab shows the climate of the chosen place, month by month: temperature from NASA POWER (2015-2025, whole country) and, around our six demo areas, vegetation greenness (NDVI) from NASA MODIS, shown next to CHIRPS rainfall. Only real, quality-checked satellite measurements are used.

It supports the Field Shift challenge by helping farmers adapt to changing conditions with open data. It is advisory only: it does not replace local agronomic advice, and it shows its assumptions and data sources.
details:
What it does: NextCrop recommends crop-rotation options for a chosen location and current crop. It always includes the current crop as a baseline and compares at least two alternatives, with plain-language benefits (e.g. nitrogen from legumes, breaking pest cycles) and risks, plus a trade-off against the baseline. Users can change assumptions (number of seasons, gaps between crops, priorities). Land suitability comes from FAO GAEZ v5 (5 arc-minute cells), covering all 24 crops we model.

How NASA data is used: the NASA tab shows monthly climate of the selected place. Temperature (T2M, T2M_MIN, T2M_MAX) comes from NASA POWER on a 0.5-degree grid across Vietnam, averaged over 2015-2025. For six demo areas we add NASA MODIS MOD13Q1 NDVI (measured, quality-checked composites only; interpolated values are excluded) next to CHIRPS rainfall. We also processed NASA SMAP soil moisture and NASA GIBS imagery in our data pipeline. These values are long-term averages, not forecasts, and do not drive the rotation ranking, which is based on FAO GAEZ.

Tools: Python (FastAPI, read-only API), PostgreSQL (Neon), plain JavaScript with MapLibre GL for the map and hand-written SVG charts, Docker and Kubernetes (k3s) for hosting.

Impact: farmers and advisers get a transparent starting point for rotation decisions as conditions change, with every assumption and source visible. Limits are stated in the app: coarse cells (not field-level), province boundaries from 2008, advisory only.
